facts.statement: Thalattosuchus measured between 3 and 4.5 meters in length, a size similar to modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Measuring 3 – 4.5 m in length, Thalattosuchus was similar in size to modern crocodiles.

facts.statement: Thalattosuchus possessed nasal salt glands used to remove excess salt from its body.
facts.quote: Thalattosuchus had nasal salt glands which, like the salt glands of all other marine reptiles, were used to remove excess salt.

facts.statement: Recent examination of fossil specimens shows that adult Thalattosuchus superciliosus had well-developed glands to eliminate excess salt from their bodies.
facts.quote: Un examen reciente de los especímenes fósiles de la especie Thalattosuchus superciliosus han mostrado que los adultos tenían glándulas bien desarrolladas para eliminar el exceso de sal de sus cuerpos.

facts.statement: Thalattosuchus was a versatile and opportunistic predator that hunted armored belemnites, fast and elusive fish, and larger species like the filter-feeding fish Leedsichthys.
facts.quote: Thalattosuchus fue un depredador versátil y oportunista, cazando tanto belemnites acorazados, como peces rápidos y escurridizos y especies más grandes como el pez filtrador Leedsichthys.

facts.statement: Thalattosuchus occasionally attempted to capture flying animals like pterosaurs and fed on plesiosaur carcasses on the sea floor.
facts.quote: Ocasionalmente debió tratar de capturar animales voladores como los pterosaurios así como alimentarse de cadáveres de plesiosaurios en el suelo marino.

facts.statement: Despite being an effective predator, Thalattosuchus was vulnerable to larger predators like the 10-meter-long pliosaur Liopleurodon.
facts.quote: A pesar de que el Thalattosuchus era un depredador efectivo, no dejaba de ser vulnerable a los mayores depredadores de su tiempo como el pliosaurio Liopleurodon, el cual podía llegar a medir algo más de 10 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Because Thalattosuchus lost the osteoderms (bony shields) characteristic of other crocodiles to become more efficient swimmers, it likely had few natural defenses against larger marine predators.
facts.quote: Dado que el Thalattosuchus había perdido ya los osteodermos (escudos óseos) característicos de otros cocodrilos, para volverse nadadores más eficientes, debió haber tenido pocas defensas naturales contra depredadores marinos mayores.

facts.statement: Although the genus Thalattosuchus was named in 2020, its fossils were historically classified under the species Metriorhynchus superciliosus.
facts.quote: Though the genus Thalattosuchus itself was named in 2020, its fossils have historically been included under the well known name Metriorhynchus as the species M. superciliosus, from which much of the research on the latter genus has been based upon.

facts.statement: In 2020, a team led by Mark Young named Thalattosuchus for the species M. superciliosus, arguing that the name Metriorhynchus should only apply to M. geoffroyii.
facts.quote: M. superciliosus was named as its own genus after a team of palaeontologists led by Mark Young in 2020 argued that the name Metriorhynchus could only be definitively applied to the type species, M. geoffroyii, and named Thalattosuchus ("sea crocodile", and from its parent group Thalattosuchia).

facts.statement: Fossil specimens of Thalattosuchus are known from Middle to Late Jurassic deposits in England, France, and Germany.
facts.quote: Fossil specimens referrable to Thalattosuchus are known from Middle-Late Jurassic deposits of England, France and Germany.

facts.statement: Fossil specimens of Thalattosuchus are known from Middle Jurassic deposits in France and England.
facts.quote: Los especímenes fósiles referibles al Thalattosuchus son conocidos de depósitos del Jurásico Medio de Francia y Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The genus Thalattosuchus was established by Young et al. in 2020.
Thalattosuchus was previously assigned to Metriorhynchus as M. superciliosus, but a 2020 cladistic analysis by Young et al. led to the creation of a new genus for it.
facts.quote: Thalattosuchus fue asignado anteriormente a Metriorhynchus, como M. superciliosus, pero el análisis cladístico de Metriorhynchidae por Young et al. (2020) impulsó la erección de un nuevo género para M. superciliosus.

facts.statement: Not all researchers accept the split; in 2022, a team led by Jonas le Mort proposed synonymizing Thalattosuchus back into Metriorhynchus.
facts.quote: Not all researchers have accepted this split, and in 2022 another team led by Jonas le Mort have proposed Thalattosuchus be syonymised back into Metriorhynchus.

facts.statement: Pellarin et al. (2026) suggest that exceptionally well-developed frontoparietal fossae in the skull of T. superciliosus may be an adaptation for surface basking to facilitate cranial heat transfer.
facts.quote: Pellarin et al. (2026) report evidence indicating that frontoparietal fossae in the skull of Thalattosuchus superciliosus were exceptionally well-developed compared to similar fossae of semi-aquatic crocodylomorphs, and interpret this difference as possibly resulting from adaptation of T. superciliosus to surface basking necessary for cranial heat transfer.

facts.statement: Thalattosuchus lived from the Callovian to the Kimmeridgian stages, approximately 165.3 to 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Kimmeridgian (165.3 to 149.2 million years ago)
